key_insight: For EHR transformers, hybrid numeric encodings that keep values but bin them before projection offer the best balance of precision, stability, and practicality, while exact arithmetic is usually not achieved.
clinical_relevance: Including laboratory values in transformer models may help some prediction tasks, but the benefit depends on the task and the encoding choice, so robust deployable designs may matter more than maximal numeric precision.
method: Compared discrete, continuous, and hybrid value-encoding strategies in transformers.
Tested on synthetic arithmetic tasks embedded in real EHR data plus real-world clinical prediction tasks.
Evaluated trade-offs in numeric precision, optimization stability, and architectural flexibility.
evidence_signal: The study combined synthetic arithmetic experiments with real-world EHR prediction tasks and found that models often learned reliable “good enough” computation rather than exact arithmetic.
watch_item: The best-performing value-encoding approach can depend on dataset size and task, so bin count and deployment settings need careful tuning before clinical use.
paper_title: How Should Transformers Encode Numeric Values in Electronic Health Records?
